@paul-j-lucas I'm able to replicate this (the cpp tag cannot be followed on dev). 

I'm seeing there's a syntax error reported from followButton.js (in the function that adds the event listeners to the follow button) - this appears to be a bug in our handling of user supplied usernames which are not escaped for json serialization (so we're sending json data that's not handled correctly by the front end - and actions that relied on processing this data are not completed)

https://github.com/forem/forem/blob/42c9a10f577a0a43673b6eafff5853d20f058240/app/javascript/packs/followButtons.js#L316 is the location where the error is reported. 

This appears to narrow down the problem on the page:

```javascript
buttons = document.querySelectorAll('.follow-action-button.follow-user:not([data-fetched])');

Array.from(buttons, (button) => { 
  console.log(button.dataset.info);
  return JSON.parse(button.dataset.info);
})
```

the console log showed a few users in order, but [one](https://dev.to/acc3ssd3n13d) (with a cpp tagged article showing on the tag page) had a name "Error401: "Name not authorized"" which was causing a parse error for the button in the code - this led to the tag's follow button having no action (it doesn't respond to the click, which is what you reported). I checked that the php tag does permit follow actions, and the 100daysofcode tag (also used by this user) does not - this narrows it down to bad input handling on our end.

This appears to be related to single escaping both the "Name not authorized" internal string and the surrounding value, causing the parser to mistakenly conclude the name string is complete after "Error401:" and try to read `Name not authorized` as json (which is invalid):

```javascript
  "{\"id\": 702615, \"className\": \"User\", \"style\": \"full\", \"name\": \"Error401:\"Name not authorized\"\"}",
```

I'm not sure if this is a problem with how we parse the data set or how we write it - the original html response includes a single quoted json string with &quot entities - which would have been valid initially:

```html
                 <div class="print-hidden">
                    <button
                      class="crayons-btn follow-action-button whitespace-nowrap follow-user w-100"
                      data-info='{"id": 702615, "className": "User", "style": "full", "name": "Error401:"Name not authorized""}'>
                      Follow
                    </button>
                  </di>v
```

The name is included in the button's data to support adding the Aria label (for accessibility) to the button (I looked at whether it could just be removed).

To widen/specify this a little further:
the broken follow functionality also applied to user pages where the user name has a quote in it, like https://dev.to/andyj115 (user name is "mi" and the follow button is broken). 

The same error appears on the [user show page](https://github.com/forem/forem/blob/main/app/views/users/show.html.erb#L38) as is present on the tag feed. In addition - if you're logged in as a user with quotes in the name, the logic to change the view's follow button to "Edit Profile" does not happen, the follow button stays "Follow" (and does not work).

The `name` field is added to button in the [story partial]( https://github.com/forem/forem/blob/main/app/views/articles/_single_story.html.erb#L65-L69 ) - and possibly also in the [MinimalProfilePreviewCard](https://github.com/forem/forem/blob/main/app/javascript/profilePreviewCards/MinimalProfilePreviewCard.jsx#L45-L50).

I suspect the erb view file is the one introducing the wrong behavior when quotes are within the string.

issue.body:
## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [x] Refactor
- [x] Bug Fix

## Description

Prior to this commit, we were somewhat naively rendering Hash style data
attributes in our ERB templates.  By rendering each hash attribute
separately, we were rendering characters that could break the
javascript (e.g. double hack or backslash `"` or `\`).

By moving to this view_object rendering, we leverage Rails's `to_json`
behavior to ensure properly escaped values.  As part of this exercise, I
generalized the method to allow for other places to benefit from this
behavior.

This generalization also helps ensure that we have a more conformant
rendering (e.g. we should always have an :id, :className, and :name
value in our data-info hash).

_Note: I've updated the user's names for Cypress tests as they are more
likely to catch the particular issue than anything else.  I assume that
I'm going to break some cypress tests and will need some help fixing
them._

## Related Tickets & Documents

Closes #15916, #14704

Supersedes #15983

## QA Instructions, Screenshots, Recordings

How to test locally:

Assuming you have seeded database (e.g. `rails db:seed`), checkout the
"main" branch.  Then in `rails console` find a user that's written articles:

```ruby

user.update(name: "\\: #{user.name}")

user.articles.each(&:save)
```

Now, again on the "main" branch, start your application (e.g.,
`bin/startup`).

Then get a logged in and a logged out browser session going.  Open your
web inspector and open console.  Then go to the local instances homepage
(e.g., http://localhost:3000) and look for JS errors.

On the main branch, you should see an exception around
`JSON.parse(button.data.info)` (assuming that the `user`'s article is
rendered on the homepage).

Then go to the user's page (e.g. https://localhost:3000/:user-slug) and
look for JS parse errors.

On this PR's branch (e.g.,
`jeremyf/take-two-at-resolving-gh-15916`)
you shouldn't see those console errors.

More importantly, the Follow buttons should work.
